questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That is was a country that did nature management and had elements that could be useful in a Danish context.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, they send all of it and there was introduction meetings. Covid was however a little bit of a problem that made everything online so not the best start.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Just some help with the IT, as always that is what can cause the most struggle. It was quite easy and a lot of the systems are very similar to KU's.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: SLU had an agreement with Bostaden which is a private housing company so it was very easy. SLU gave me a key and then I just had to find the room at it is pretty okay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: it is not very social at the student corridors you live at. Do not expect the same social life as in danish kollegier. But you will have a good social life outside of the corridor so it is not a problem.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was kinda easy. It is very similar to the KU system.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The teachers and the international student service people.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is not difficult, the professors can always help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took master level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar to the style of KU. Some professors were however significantly better than others in terms of teaching and assignment giving.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Human dimensions of wildlife management
2. Fish and wildlife management.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend the human dimensions course. It is something we do not have at KU like that in any way. It will give you some very nice perspectives!
Also the fish and wildlife management was really good. Again something we do not have in Denmark at that level! If you like wildlife and want to know more then this is the SLU is the place to go.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you have a car, you have to pay for parking every month. 120 kr.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is relatively similar to DK prices. Although some vegetables are more expensive than in DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The only thing I really used was the student bar, Skogis. Super nice place with cheap beer and a good vibe. The thursday pub night is the best! 
They also have other unions but I think it is better if you stay for more than 1 semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is also this place called IKSU which has everything in fitness/sports. A great bouldering place and 1000 classes from yoga to spinning if you want to stay in shape like that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to the national parks! Skule skogen and Bjornlandet are really good and not too far away. You do need a car though to reach it. 
Go skiing in the winter! You can rent all sorts of outdoor equipment at Fritidsbanken for free! it is very close to the student housing in Ålidhem.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Swedish and danish culture is not that different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: have a coffee with the Swedes in the coffee break! talk to them and at some point they will open up and they are super nice people! Also go to alle the parties and "Sitnings".

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Just that it takes time to get to know the Swedes

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: they are very friendly

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy the nature around Umeå
Go do things with the locals
If you have a car, bring it!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of stuff is very similar to KU so it is easy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural exchange and the good outdoor life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was pretty good. I had no major challenges.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
